evidence_set: Because the norketamine areas after the oral and intravenous conditions were similar once corrected for dose, the authors attribute the low oral ketamine concentrations to first-pass metabolism rather than to poor absorption (2nd paragraph); they compare their intravenous half-life with the 151 minutes reported after anaesthetic amounts (2.5 mg/kg) in patients, against 186 minutes at the analgesic amounts studied here (1st paragraph); and they report norketamine concentrations up to 390 ng/mL in some people after the oral solution (4th paragraph, the Results giving the oral range as 80 to 390 ng/mL on the same page).

Norketamine exposure differs sharply by preparation: area to 8 hours 173.8 and 149.8 ng·h/mL for the (R)- and (S)-enantiomer after the 20 mg injection against 533.8 and 494.9 after the 50 mg swallowed tablet, in the same three men. The authors describe the tablet's norketamine area as approximately eight times the ketamine area to infinity and read it as extensive first-pass metabolism; the printed values give 7.4 and 7.6 (editors' recomputation: 533.8 divided by 72.3 and 494.9 divided by 64.9).

evidence_set: In its 2nd paragraph the review states that the two forms have similar pharmacokinetic profiles but different effects: some studies indicate the S-form may be about four times more potent than the R-form as an analgesic in humans while producing more auditory and visual disturbances, R-ketamine produces more agitation in surgical patients, emergence is faster after S-ketamine than after the R-form or the racemate, and the difference in analgesic efficiency is explained by S-ketamine's four times higher affinity for the NMDA receptor. The 1st paragraph gives effective concentrations for loss of consciousness of 241 ng/mL (SD 90) for the racemate and 111 (SD 30) for S-ketamine, taken from a textbook chapter.
Section 6 Pharmacodynamics and Clinical Use of Ketamine, 1st and 2nd paragraphs

In three healthy men, no pharmacokinetic parameter of ketamine or norketamine differed significantly between the (R)- and the (S)-enantiomer, or between the five preparations, by analysis of variance (named in the Methods on p. 39 with 0.05 as the minimal level of significance). No test statistic, degrees of freedom or p-value is printed anywhere in the paper, so this null result in three people cannot be read as evidence that the two forms behave alike in the body.

evidence_set: Norketamine exposure in three healthy men, (R)- then (S)-enantiomer: 533.8 and 494.9 ng·h/mL after the swallowed tablet, 462.9 and 408.7 after the sublingual tablet, 322.6 and 282.6 after the suppository, 173.8 and 149.8 after the injection, and 115.9 and 100.7 after the nasal spray. The nasal pair is headed as the area to 8 hours in Table 2 but called the area to 6 hours in the abstract and the Discussion, because norketamine was below the detection limit 8 hours after the spray, so that pair is integrated over a shorter window than the other four. The reading that the nasal route largely escapes first-pass metabolism is the authors', stated in the Discussion on p. 42, not in the table.
